note: The evidence relation merged to master in #130 but did not reach PyPI, and neither did #128/#129. release-please cuts a version only from conventional-commit prefixes (feat/fix/security/perf/refactor/build/deps), and every PR title since v0.4.0 was prose ('Evidence: the axis...', 'Edge-confirmation ceremony...'), so release-please ran green and proposed nothing. Verified: release-please run 32065642320 on the #130 merge = success; no open 'chore(master): release' PR; PyPI nestor-meaning still 0.4.0; latest tag v0.4.0. This PR adds a real read-only CLI action, `nestor evidence for <pair_id>`, under a feat: title, so release-please opens the 0.5.0 release PR and the already-merged evidence work ships with it.

decisions.question: The evidence work is merged but not on PyPI. Why, and what actually carries it there?
decisions.commitment: A conventional-commit title does. release-please reads the release-cutting type from PR titles and commits (the title lands in the merge-commit body, docs/releasing.md); #128/#129/#130 all used prose titles, so no release was proposed and PyPI stayed at 0.4.0. This PR ships a genuine feat -- a `nestor evidence for <pair_id>` read action -- titled `feat:`, which makes release-please open 'chore(master): release 0.5.0'. release-please tags from current master HEAD, so everything merged since v0.4.0, the evidence relation included, ships in that build.
decisions.why: Forcing a release with an empty trigger commit or a Release-As footer would work but would be a lie about what changed; a real feat under a correct title is the mechanism working as designed rather than routed around. The lesson is worth keeping because it is invisible until it bites: a feature can be fully merged, tested, and green and still never leave the repo, with no error anywhere, because its title was prose. The fix is a habit (title the PR by its release type), and the record is here so the next feature is not stranded the same way.
decisions.doors_closed: Pushing a release tag from this session (an agent's credentials refuse refs/tags/*, HTTP 403, and docs/releasing.md removes the manual path). An empty or Release-As trigger commit (a real feat is honest where a trigger is not).

decisions.question: What is the feat, and is it real product surface or a pretext?
decisions.commitment: Real. `nestor evidence for <pair_id>` lists the references attached to one pair -- the read that completes the CLI triad (attach writes, report queues the unevidenced, for reads one pair's evidence). It wraps evidence.evidence_for, which existed in the library with no CLI door. Read-only, exits 0, prints kind/locator/reason/attached_by or 'no evidence attached'. A CLI test locks it.
decisions.why: The evidence CLI shipped with a write (attach) and an aggregate read (report) but no way to see what a single pair rests on without a Python call -- a genuine gap a curator hits the first time they want to inspect one row. Filling it is worth doing on its own merits, which is exactly why it is the right thing to carry the release: the trigger and the improvement are the same change, so nothing ships that was not wanted for itself.
decisions.doors_closed: A CLI action that could mutate under 'for' (it is strictly read-only, like report).
